subject: Class 158 Express Sprinter, 2-car (cab car + other driving car), six operators
method: Side elevation from the Vauxhallvauxhall Northern diagram (all diagrams in the series share its template pixel for pixel), axes calibrated separately; heights checked against two photos (photo wins on window and line heights); window positions cross-checked by 1D projective fits through the door edges on two photos; face from the 159012 head-on photo; liveries from each operator's diagram (EM from photos: no current diagram); colours sampled.

calibration.notes: Horizontal: gangway frame front px 31 to car end px 1706 = 1675 px = 22.57 m (published car length) -> 74.2 px/m (the next car 1760-3434 = 1674 px agrees). If 22.57 m is over the body only (px 52-1706), the scale is 73.3 px/m (1.3% less): this is the main length uncertainty. x = 0 is the body face at px 52; the gangway frame stands 0.30 m proud of it. Vertical: rail (wheel bottom) row 339 to roof top row 31 = 308 px = 3.73 m (published) -> 82.6 px/m, 11% more than horizontally: the drawing is stretched vertically. The diagram's heights between 1.0 and 2.1 m read about 0.1 m high against two photos (see trace heights.window and liveries.GW).

trace.liveries.roof: Roof colours: every roof sample is the roof's top seen lit by the sky above it, which on an overcast or open sky is about 2.5 times the light the bodyside gets (CIE overcast sky: horizontal over vertical illuminance ~2.5), so a roof read straight off the photo renders near white (first render). Each roof is its sample's median divided by 2.5 in linear light: GW gw-roof median #D0CFD5 -> #8A898D; NT nt-roof median #9EAEC1 -> #67727F; EM emr-roof median #A6AAAA -> #6D7070; SR sr-roof median #F6F7FA -> #A3A4A6; SW sw-roof median #D1D1D5 -> #8A8A8D; AW keeps the diagram's #808080 (its sample spread is 125-140, unusable). Stage A's gw-roof box sits on the roof (roof158 grid), not the canopy.

trace.model.cab.x: cab-car positions along the train, fifth pass: the diagram draws the cab end too short. Two photos put the face further ahead of door 1 than the diagram: pemr (158866 nearly side-on), a 1D projective fit along the bodyside through door 1's edges and nine window fronts (residuals 0-12 cm, typically 3) puts the face's side corner at -0.25 m and the cab window 0.12-0.90 m in the diagram's frame, i.e. the face 0.40 m further forward (its side corner is 0.15 m behind the tip); pgw (camera from the bodyside, lamps held out) wants the face 0.47-0.65 m forward, less reliably (its lamps come out 0.17 m apart in height left to right, so it is not pinned off the side). Applied: 0.40 m, the cab section 0..1.267 m stretched to 0..1.667 m (the cab side window and the cab-end paint with it) and everything from door 1 back moved 0.40 m; the cab car is 0.40 m longer (22.69 m, against 22.57 published over the gangway frame: the remaining 0.12 m is within the diagram's scale doubt).

The first two builds drew it 1.06-0.84 m wide from 1.05 m: read off the wider shadow ; checked through the pgw camera: the opening traced on the photo at full resolution, top 550-805 px at row 1330, foot 580-770 at row 1500, and ours projected, top 569-801 at 1332-1340, foot 610-752 at ~1497: within 30 px (~9 cm) everywhere

notes.fleet: GW: 13 x 2-car + 5 x 3-car (158/0, 158/7, 158/9 ex-Northern); NT: 35 x 2-car + 8 x 3-car (158/0, 158/8, 158/9); EM: 26 x 2-car; SR: 40 x 2-car 158/7; AW: 22 x 2-car 158/8 (last Cambrian workings spring 2026, geograph 8320761); SW: 10 x 2-car 158/8 (158880-890). Wikipedia infobox/fleet table. All sub-classes share the body; differences are engines, interiors and (on 3-car sets) the extra car, not the outside shape this spec draws. The 3-car GW/NT sets' middle car is not measured.
